attribution: Nellyrieuf — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Matho Monastery rising above the snow-covered Indus valley in winter.
caption: Matho Monastery in winter. Its Nagrang festival, with the village's two oracles, falls around 19-20 February 2027 and anchors the middle of this route in the coldest, quietest season of the Ladakhi year.

commonsFile: File:A snow leopard wild Ladakh DSCN4780 02.jpg
attribution: T. R. Shankar Raman — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A wild female snow leopard resting on a rocky slope in Ladakh.
caption: A wild snow leopard resting in Ladakh. February is the peak sighting season around Rumbak and Ulley, but sightings are never guaranteed: the realistic goal is several days of patient glassing with local spotters.

attribution: Karunakar Rayker — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A bharal (blue sheep) standing on a dry mountain slope in Hemis National Park.
caption: Bharal, the blue sheep that is the snow leopard's main prey in Hemis. Finding herds on the slopes above Rumbak is how spotters locate the cats, and bharal and ibex are reliable sightings even when the leopard stays hidden.

photographer: Chris Hunkeler from Carlsbad, California, USA
attribution: Chris Hunkeler from Carlsbad, California, USA — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A traditional flat-roofed homestay house in Rumbak village in the Ladakhi mountains.
caption: A homestay house in Rumbak, the village that has hosted snow leopard watchers since the community homestay scheme began. Guests sleep in family houses, eat in the kitchen around the stove and pay the household directly.

attribution: Gozitano — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A broad mountain valley with steep ridges in Hemis National Park.
caption: A valley in Hemis High Altitude National Park, the protected area south of Leh where the Rumbak gorge is reached on foot from the Zingchen road end. In February it is snowbound and the walk in is part of the expedition.

attribution: Prof Ranga Sai — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Stok Monastery, a white-walled Buddhist monastery in the Indus valley near Leh.
caption: Stok Monastery, 15 km from Leh, host of the Guru Tsechu masked-dance and oracle festival expected on 15-16 February 2027. The village homestays here are the first night away from Leh.

attribution: RPSkokie — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Leh Palace and old town, Leh
alt: The nine-storey Leh Palace above the old town of Leh in morning light.
caption: Leh Palace above the old town. Leh sits at 3,500 m and the group spends its first three days here, because the district administration requires 48 hours of acclimatisation before travelling to higher ground.

attribution: Ingo Mehling — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Likir Monastery on a hillside above the Sham valley in Ladakh.
caption: Likir Monastery in the Sham valley, on the way to Ulley's snow leopard slopes. It is a working Gelug monastery where winter visits mean empty courtyards and monks who have time to talk.

commonsFile: File:Lamayuru Monastery with Moonland in the Background.jpg
attribution: Kushaldonde — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Lamayuru Monastery on a ridge above eroded clay hills known as the Moonland.
caption: Lamayuru Monastery above its eroded lake-bed 'Moonland'. In February the monastery is nearly empty and the village is a quiet overnight stop on the western Sham loop.

attribution: Deepank Ranka — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Wanla Gompa on a ridge above Wanla village in a narrow Ladakhi gorge.
caption: Wanla Gompa crowning its ridge above the gorge south of Lamayuru. The road to Wanla follows a narrow canyon that ices over in February, so the detour depends on a driver who knows its winter condition.

attribution: Goutam1962 — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Zanskar River, Chadar route near Tibb
alt: Trekkers walking on the frozen Zanskar River between snowy canyon walls on the Chadar route.
caption: The Chadar, the frozen Zanskar River. It was suspended in 2026 because the ice did not form; it is not in the plan and is shown to document what is at stake and why it is excluded.

attribution: Tashi Ldawa — CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: A Himalayan ibex standing on a rocky slope beside the Zanskar River.
caption: A Himalayan ibex, one of the animals you can see from the road in winter, when snow drives herds down toward villages. Ibex are the most reliable wildlife of the Leh-Alchi-Lamayuru road.
